metadata.title: Dirac cohomology, the projective supermodules of the symmetric group and the Vogan morphism

nodes.name: fixed real root system and Weyl group $W$
nodes.statement: We fix a real root system $\{V, \Phi, V^\vee, \Phi^\vee\}$, where $\Phi$ is the set of roots inside the real vector space $V$, we have a perfect bilinear pairing $B( \ , \ ) : V \times V^\vee \to \mathbb{R}$ The roots are in bijections with the coroots such that $B( \alpha , \alpha^\vee ) = 2$. We define reflections $$s_\alpha : V \to V, \hspace{0.75cm} s_\alpha (v) = v - B( v, \alpha^\vee )\alpha.$$ Let $W$ be the subgroup of $GL(V)$ generated by the reflections $s_\alpha$ for all $\alpha \in \Phi$. Fix a $W$-invariant bilinear form on $V$, $( \ , \ )$ on $V$, a set of positive (resp. simple) roots $\Phi^+$ (resp. $\Pi$). The reflections $s_\alpha$ for $\alpha \in \Pi$ generate $W$.
nodes.statement_short: Standing setup: a real root system, its reflections, the Weyl group $W$, a $W$-invariant form and a choice of positive/simple roots.

nodes.name: the automorphism $\delta$ and the extension $W_\#$
nodes.statement: We let $\delta$ denote the automorphism $W$ given by the conjugation by $w_0$ on $V$, where $w_0$ is the longest element in $W$. Then let $W_\#$ be the extension of $W$ by $\delta$. Explicitly $$W_\# = \langle W , \delta : \delta^2 = 1, \delta w \delta = \delta(w) \text{ for all } w \in W \rangle.$$
differentia: $\delta$ denote the automorphism $W$ given by the conjugation by $w_0$ on $V$

nodes.name: graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb{H}$
nodes.statement: The graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb{H}$ associated to a Weyl group $W$, $V$ and $( \ ,\ )$ is the associative unital $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by $\{ \xi \in V\}$ and $\{w\in W\}$ such that there exist injections, induced by the inclusion of generators, $$S(V) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H},$$ $$\mathbb{C}[W] \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H}.$$ Furthermore, for every simple root $\alpha \in \Pi$, there exist cross-relations, $$\xi \cdot s_\alpha - s_\alpha \cdot s_\alpha(\xi) = ( \alpha , \xi ).$$
nodes.statement_short: The graded Hecke algebra of $W$: $S(V)$ and $\mathbb{C}[W]$ glued by the cross-relation $\xi s_\alpha - s_\alpha s_\alpha(\xi) = (\alpha,\xi)$.
differentia: there exist injections, induced by the inclusion of generators, $S(V) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H},$ $\mathbb{C}[W] \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H}$
for every simple root $\alpha \in \Pi$, there exist cross-relations, $\xi \cdot s_\alpha - s_\alpha \cdot s_\alpha(\xi) = ( \alpha , \xi )$

nodes.name: the extended graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb{H}_\#$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathbb{H}_\#$ to be an extension of the graded Hecke algebra by $\delta$. Explicitly, $$ \mathbb{H}_\# = \langle \mathbb{H} , \delta \rangle = \langle \mathbb{H}, \delta : \delta^2 = 1, \delta h \delta = \delta(h) \text{ for all } h \in \mathbb{H} \rangle. $$ As a vector space $\mathbb{H}_\#$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{H} \oplus \mathbb{H}$.
nodes.genus: an extension of the graded Hecke algebra by $\delta$
differentia: As a vector space $\mathbb{H}_\#$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{H} \oplus \mathbb{H}$

nodes.name: Clifford algebra $C(V)$
nodes.statement: The Clifford algebra $C(V)$ defined by $V$ and the symmetric bilinear form $( \ , \ )$ on $V$ is the associative unital algebra generated by elements in $V$ such that $$\xi\xi' + \xi'\xi = 2( \xi' , \xi ) \text{ for all } \xi, \xi' \in V.$$
nodes.genus: associative unital algebra generated by elements in $V$

nodes.name: filtration, $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-grading, transpose and $\epsilon$ on $C(V)$
nodes.statement: The Clifford algebra has a natural filtration by $\mathbb{Z}$. Each generator is given degree one and then $C(V)_n$ is the span of all elements of $C(V)$ with degree $n$ or lower. $C(V)$ also has a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ grading, $$C(V) = C(V)_{\even}\oplus C(V)_{\odd}$$ where $C(V)_{\even}$ is the span of all homogeneous elements of even degree and likewise for $C(V)_{\odd}$. Define the transpose of $C(V)$ be the antiautomorphism defined by $\xi^t = -\xi$ for all elements of $V$ and let $\epsilon: C(V) \to C(V)$ to the involution which is the identity on $C(V)_{\even}$ and acts as $-1$ on $C(V)_{\odd}$.
nodes.statement_short: The Clifford algebra carries a $\mathbb{Z}$-filtration, a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-grading, a transpose antiautomorphism and the parity involution $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Pin group $Pin(V)$
nodes.statement: The Pin group is $$Pin(V) = \{g\in C(V)^\times | g^t = g^{-1} \text{ and } \epsilon(g) \xi g^{-1} \in V, \text{ for all } \xi \in V\}.$$

nodes.name: the projection $p$ and the double cover $\tilde{W} = p^{-1}(W)$
nodes.statement: This group is a double cover of the orthogonal group on $V$ with projection $p: Pin(V) \to O(V)$, $$p(g)(\xi) = \epsilon(g)\xi g^{-1}.$$ Since the Weyl group is a subgroup of $O(V)$ we can find a double cover of $W$ in the pin group. Let $\tilde{W}$ be the preimage of $W$ via $p$, $$\tilde{W} = p^{-1} (W).$$
nodes.statement_short: The Pin group double-covers $O(V)$ via $p$, and $\tilde{W}:=p^{-1}(W)$ is the resulting double cover of the Weyl group.

nodes.name: $\tilde{W}_\#$, $\omega$, $\tilde{W}'$ and $\tilde{W}_\#'$
nodes.statement: As a subgroup of $O(V)$, we have $W_\# = \langle W ,\delta\rangle$ is equal to $\langle W, -1\rangle$. Hence we can also define $\tilde{W}_\# = p^{-1}(W_\#)$. The non scalar element in the preimage of $-1$ is $\omega$ which can be formulated in terms of an orthonormal basis $\{\xi_1,\ldots ,\xi_n\}$ of $V$, as $$\omega = \xi_1\xi_2\ldots \xi_n \in Pin(V).$$ We will also define $\tilde{W}'$ and $\tilde{W}_\#'$ to be $$\tilde{W}' = \begin{cases} \tilde{W} \cap C(V)_{\even}, & \dim V \text{ even }, \\ \tilde{W}, & \dim V \text{ odd }, \end{cases}$$ and $$\tilde{W}_\#' = \begin{cases} \langle \tilde{W} \cap C(V)_{\even}, \omega \rangle, & \dim V even, \\ \tilde{W}_\#, & \dim V odd. \end{cases}$$
nodes.statement_short: Defines $\tilde{W}_\# = p^{-1}(W_\#)$, the element $\omega = \xi_1\cdots\xi_n$, and the even-part restrictions $\tilde{W}'$, $\tilde{W}_\#'$ used when $\dim V$ is even.

nodes.name: twisted group algebra $\mathcal{T}_n$ of $S_n$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the twisted group algebra of $S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$. Explicitly $\mathcal{T}_n$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by $\tau_i$ for $i = 1 \ldots n-1$ such that $$\tau_i^2 = 1, (\tau_i \tau_j)^{m(i,j)} = (-1)^{m(i,j)-1}.$$

nodes.name: genuine projective irreducible representations of $\tilde{S}_n$
nodes.statement: The genuine projective irreducible representations of $\tilde{S}_n$ are the irreducible representations that do not descend to a representation of $S_n$. The group algebra for $\tilde{S}_n$ decomposes as $$\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n] \cong \mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]/(z -1) \oplus \mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n ]/(z+1) \cong \mathbb{C}[S_n] \oplus \mathcal{T}_n.$$ If we are interested in the projective representations of $\tilde{S}_n$, i.e. those that do not occurs as representations of $S_n$, then we just need to study the representations of $\mathcal{T}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Genuine projective irreducibles are those not descending to $S_n$; since $\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]\cong\mathbb{C}[S_n]\oplus\mathcal{T}_n$, they are exactly the $\mathcal{T}_n$-representations.
differentia: that do not descend to a representation of $S_n$

nodes.name: vector superspace and superalgebra
nodes.statement: A vector superspace is a vector space $U$ which is $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, $U = U_0 \oplus U_1$. Similarly, a superalgebra is an algebra which is $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded.

nodes.name: $\End(U)$ as a superalgebra
nodes.statement: For a vector superspace $U$ we can define $\End(U)$ to be isomorphic to $\End(U_0 \oplus U_1)$ as an ungraded algebra then as a superalgebra the even elements fix $U_i$ and odd elements take $U_0$ to $U_1$ and $U_1$ to $U_0$.
differentia: as a superalgebra the even elements fix $U_i$ and odd elements take $U_0$ to $U_1$ and $U_1$ to $U_0$

nodes.name: supermodule of a superalgebra
nodes.statement: A supermodule of a superalgebra $A$ is a super vector space $U$ along with a graded map from $A \to End(U)$.
differentia: along with a graded map from $A \to End(U)$

nodes.name: type M and type Q supermodules
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be an $A$-supermodule. Then $U$ is of type M if, when one forgets the grading, $U$ is an irreducible $A$ ungraded module. The module $U$ is of type Q if it is reducible as an $A$ ungraded module.
differentia: type M if, when one forgets the grading, $U$ is an irreducible $A$ ungraded module
type Q if it is reducible as an $A$ ungraded module

nodes.name: supertrace $\str_V$
nodes.statement: The supertrace on the representation $U= U_0 \oplus U_1$ is defined to be zero on odd elements and, on even elements, $$\str_V(a) = \tr_0 (a) - \tr_1(a)$$ where $tr_i(a)$ is the trace of the matrix corresponding to $a$ restricted to $U_i$.
nodes.genus: a trace on the representation $U = U_0\oplus U_1$
differentia: defined to be zero on odd elements

nodes.name: partition, length of a partition, strict partition
nodes.statement: We will use three different types of partitions throughout. Let $\lambda = (\lambda_1,..,\lambda_r) \in \mathbb{N}^r$. The set $\lambda$ is a partition of $n$ if $\sum_{i=1}^r \lambda_i = n$ and $\lambda_1\geq \lambda_2 \geq \ldots \geq \lambda_r$. We will denote the set of partitions of $n$ by $\mathcal{P}(n)$. We define the length of a partition, $l(\lambda)$, to be $\#\{\lambda_i : \lambda_i > 0\}$ We say a partition $\lambda \vdash n$ is strict if $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\ldots >\lambda_r$.
nodes.statement_short: Partition, its length $l(\lambda)$, and the notion of a strict partition (strictly decreasing parts).

nodes.name: Young diagram of a partition
nodes.statement: For a partition $\lambda \vdash n$ we associate to it a set of boxes forming the Young diagram. For $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r)$, we define the Young diagram to be $$\lambda = \{ (i,j) : 1 < i < l(\lambda) \text{ and } 1< j < \lambda_i \}.$$
nodes.genus: a set of boxes associated to a partition $\lambda \vdash n$

nodes.name: shifted partition and $\mathcal{SP}(n)$
nodes.statement: The set of shifted partitions of $n$ is the same as the set of strict partitions of $n$. However, we will consider a different $Young$ diagram for a shifted partition than the associated Young diagram of a normal partition. We will write $\lambda \vDash n$ to denote a shifted partition of $n$ and $\mathcal{SP}(n)$ is the set of shifted partitions of $n$.
nodes.genus: the set of strict partitions of $n$
differentia: we will consider a different $Young$ diagram for a shifted partition than the associated Young diagram of a normal partition

nodes.name: shifted Young diagram
nodes.statement: Given a shifted partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r) \vDash n$ we associate a shifted Young diagram, $$\lambda = \{ (i,j) : 1 < i < l(\lambda) \text{ and } i< j < i+ \lambda_i -1 \}.$$
nodes.genus: a diagram associated to a shifted partition $\lambda \vDash n$
differentia: $\lambda = \{ (i,j) : 1 < i < l(\lambda) \text{ and } i< j < i+ \lambda_i -1 \}$

nodes.name: (standard) Young tableau and shifted Young tableau
nodes.statement: A Young tableau of shape $\lambda$ is a numbering of $1$ to $n$ of the Young diagram associated to $\lambda$. We will write $[\lambda]$ for a Young tableau of shape $\lambda$. Similarly $[[\lambda]]$ will denote a numbering of the shifted Young diagram associated to $\lambda \vDash n$. A standard Young tableau (resp. shifted) is a Young tableau (resp. shifted) such that along each row and column the numbers increase.
nodes.statement_short: Numberings $[\lambda]$, $[[\lambda]]$ of (shifted) Young diagrams; standard means rows and columns increase.
nodes.genus: a Young tableau (resp. shifted) of shape $\lambda$
differentia: a numbering of $1$ to $n$ of the Young diagram associated to $\lambda$
along each row and column the numbers increase

nodes.name: conjugate partition $\lambda'$
nodes.statement: Given a partition $\lambda$ we write $\lambda'$ for its conjugate partition, which is the reflection of the Young diagram in its main diagonal.
differentia: the reflection of the Young diagram in its main diagonal

nodes.name: diagonal embedding $\rho$ of $\tilde{W}_\#$
nodes.statement: Let $\rho$ be the diagonal embedding of $\tilde{W}_\#$ into $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$; $$\rho (w) = p(w) \otimes w, \text{ for all } w \in \tilde{W}_\#.$$ Hence, for an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module $X$ and a spinor module $\mathcal{S}$, we can consider $X\otimes \mathcal{S}$ as a $\tilde{W}_\#$-module via the map $\rho$.
nodes.statement_short: $\rho(w) = p(w)\otimes w$ embeds $\tilde{W}_\#$ diagonally in $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$, making $X\otimes\mathcal{S}$ a $\tilde{W}_\#$-module.
nodes.genus: the diagonal embedding of $\tilde{W}_\#$ into $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$

nodes.name: the anti-automorphism $*$ and $\tilde{\xi}$
nodes.statement: Let $*$ be the linear anti-automorphism on $\mathbb{H}$ defined by $$w^* = w^{-1}, \xi^* = w_0 \delta(\xi)w_0, \text{ for all } w\in W \text{ and } \xi \in V.$$ We can extend $*$ to $\mathbb{H}_\#$ by defining it to fix $\delta$. Given $\xi$, let $$\tilde{\xi} = \frac{1}{2}(\xi - \xi^*).$$
differentia: $w^* = w^{-1}, \xi^* = w_0 \delta(\xi)w_0, \text{ for all } w\in W \text{ and } \xi \in V$
extend $*$ to $\mathbb{H}_\#$ by defining it to fix $\delta$

nodes.name: Dirac element $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement: Let $\{\xi_1,\ldots ,\xi_n\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $V$. The Dirac element $\mathcal{D}$ in $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$ is defined to be, $$\mathcal{D} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde{\xi}_i \otimes \xi_i.$$

nodes.name: extended Dirac cohomology $H^D_\#(X)$
nodes.statement: The extended Dirac cohomology of $X$ (with respect to $\mathcal{S}$) is $$H^D_\#(X) = \ker(D_\#) / \ker(D_\#)\cap \im(D_\#).$$ This is a $\tilde{W}_\#$ representation since $\tilde{W}_\#$ commutes with $\mathcal{D}$. We are also interested in the restriction of $D_\#$ to the even and odd spaces. The subspace $X\otimes \mathcal{S}^\pm$ is always a $\tilde{W}_\#'$-module. Let, $$H^{D^\pm}_\#(X) = \ker(D^\pm_\#) / \ker(D^\pm_\#)\cap \im(D^\mp_\#).$$ Note that when $\dim V$ is even $X\otimes \mathcal{S}^\pm$ is not an $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$-module, just an $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)_{\even}$-module. The space $H^{D^\pm}_\#(X)$ is a $\tilde{W}_\#'$-module.
nodes.statement_short: $H^D_\#(X) = \ker D_\# / (\ker D_\# \cap \im D_\#)$, a $\tilde{W}_\#$-representation, together with its graded pieces $H^{D^\pm}_\#(X)$.

nodes.name: extended Dirac index $I_\#(X)$
nodes.statement: The extended Dirac index is $$I_\#(X) = H^{D^+}_\#(X) - H^{D^-}_\#(X)$$ defined as a virtual $\tilde{W}_\#'$-module.

nodes.name: the Borel variety $\mathcal{B}_e$ and Springer's $W$-action
nodes.statement: It will be useful to introduce a certain graded module. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Weyl group $W$. Then, for an element $e$ in the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N}$, we let $\mathcal{B}_e$ denote the variety of Borel subalgebras of $\mathfrak{g}$ containing $e$. Springer \cite{S78} defined a $W$ action on the cohomology groups $H^j(\mathcal{B}_e)$. The cohomology $H^j(\mathcal{B}_e)$ vanishes unless $j$ is even.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{B}_e$ is the variety of Borel subalgebras containing a nilpotent $e$; Springer's $W$-action lives on $H^j(\mathcal{B}_e)$, which vanishes for odd $j$.
nodes.genus: the variety of Borel subalgebras of $\mathfrak{g}$
differentia: $e$ an element in the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N}$

nodes.name: the $\textbf{q}$-graded $W$-module $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$
nodes.statement: Let $e$ be an element in the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N} \subset \mathfrak{g}$, $\mathcal{B}_e$ the variety of Borel subalgebras containing $e$ and $d_e$ be the dimension of $\mathcal{B}_e$. The sign character of $W$ will be denoted by $\sgn$. Let $\textbf{q}$ be a formal symbol. Springer \cite{S78} constructed an action of $W$ on $H^j(\mathcal{B}_e)$. Define the $\textbf{q}$-graded $W$-module. $$X_{\textbf{q}}(e) = \sum_{i \geq 0} \textbf{q}^{d_e - i} H^{2i}(\mathcal{B}_e) \otimes \sgn.$$
nodes.statement_short: $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ is the $\textbf{q}$-graded $W$-module assembled from the Springer cohomology $H^{2i}(\mathcal{B}_e)\otimes\sgn$.

nodes.name: restriction to $W = S_n$ and $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{sl}_n$
nodes.statement: From here on we will fix $W$ to be $S_n$ and $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{sl}_n$. Because of this we will take results from \cite{CH15} and restrict them to $S_n$ to avoid surplus definitions. Note that the correspondence from \cite[Appendix A]{CH15}, applies to almost any Weyl group, but outside of type A there is an extra complication involving the component group of the centraliser of $e$. In the full generality of \cite{CH15} the graded modules involved are labelled by a nilpotent element $e$ and an element in this component group. However for $S_n$ this component group is always trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Standing restriction to type A: $W=S_n$, $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}_n$, where the relevant component group is trivial.

nodes.name: Casimir element $\Omega_\mathbb{H}$ for $\mathbb{H}$
nodes.statement: The Casimir element for $\mathbb{H}$ is $$\Omega_\mathbb{H} = \sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^2,$$ where $\{\xi_i\}$ is an orthonormal basis for $V$.

nodes.name: Casimir element $\Omega_{\tilde{S_n}}$ for $\tilde{S_n}$
nodes.statement: The Casimir element for $\tilde{S_n}$ is $$\Omega_{\tilde{S_n}} = \frac{1}{4}\sum_{\begin{substack}{\alpha, \beta \in \Phi^+\\ s_\alpha(\beta) < 0} \end{substack}} |\alpha||\beta| \tau_\alpha \tau_\beta,$$ where $\tau_\alpha$ is the generator of $\tilde{S_n}$ corresponding to $\alpha$. In \cite{BCT12} $\Omega_{\tilde{S}}$ is negative but we define it as positive since we have the positive form on $C(V)$.
nodes.statement_short: The Casimir of $\tilde{S}_n$: a signed sum $\frac14\sum|\alpha||\beta|\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta$ over pairs of positive roots with $s_\alpha(\beta)<0$.
differentia: we define it as positive since we have the positive form on $C(V)$

nodes.name: Steinberg module $St$
nodes.statement: We introduce the one dimensional $\mathbb{H}$-module, called the Steinberg module $St$. Here $S_n$ acts on $St$ by the $\sgn$ character and $\xi_i\in S(V)$ act by $\frac{n-1 + 2i}{2}$.

nodes.name: the parabolically induced module $X_\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let $X_\lambda$ be the parabolically induced $\mathbb{H}$-module from the Steinberg module for $\mathbb{H}_{\lambda_1}\times \ldots \times \mathbb{H}_{\lambda_k}$, $$X_\lambda = \Ind_{\mathbb{H}_{\lambda_1}\times \ldots \times \mathbb{H}_{\lambda_k}}^\mathbb{H} (St_{\lambda_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes St_{\lambda_k}).$$

nodes.name: convention $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = 0$ for non-strict $\lambda$
nodes.statement: For ease of explanation later on in this paper, and motivated by Remark \ref{indexkilled}, we will set $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = 0$ if $\lambda$ is not a strict partition.

nodes.name: the graded character $p^\lambda(q)$
nodes.statement: Let $p^\lambda (q)$ be the character of the graded $S_n$-module $$\sum_{i\geq0} \textbf{q}^i H^{2i}(\mathcal{B}_\lambda ).$$

nodes.name: the reduction rule producing $\lambda^{(i)}$
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r)$ be a fixed partition of $n$ and $\lambda' = (\lambda_1',\ldots ,\lambda_r')$ be its conjugate. For $1 \leq i \leq l(\lambda)$ define the integer $a_i$ by the condition $$\lambda_{a_i}' \geq i > \lambda_{a_i+1}'.$$ Given this integer, let $\lambda^{(i)}$ be the partition created when one removes a block from the bottom of column $a_i$ of the Young diagram associated to $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: Garcia-Procesi reduction rule: $\lambda^{(i)}$ removes a block from the bottom of the column $a_i$ singled out by $\lambda'_{a_i}\geq i>\lambda'_{a_i+1}$.
nodes.genus: the partition created when one removes a block from the bottom of column $a_i$ of the Young diagram associated to $\lambda$

nodes.name: the box-removal set $\Theta^n_{n-1}(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Given $\lambda \vdash n$, let $\Theta^n_{n-1}(\lambda)$ be the set of partitions of $n-1$ which one can create from the Young diagram of $\lambda$ by removing a single box.
differentia: which one can create from the Young diagram of $\lambda$ by removing a single box

nodes.name: the restriction functor $\Res^n_{n-1}$
nodes.statement: Given a module or character $A$ of either $S_n$, $\tilde{S}_n$ or $C(n)$, let $\Res_{n-1}^n(A)$ denote the restriction to the rank $({n-1})$ object, that is the restriction to $S_{n-1}$, $\tilde{S}_{n-1}$ or $C(n-1)$.
nodes.genus: the restriction of a module or character $A$
differentia: to the rank $({n-1})$ object, that is the restriction to $S_{n-1}$, $\tilde{S}_{n-1}$ or $C(n-1)$

nodes.name: Jucys-Murphy elements $M_i$ in $\mathcal{T}_n$
nodes.statement: The Jucys-Murphy elements in $\mathcal{T}_n$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$ are, $$M_i = \sum_{\alpha \in \Phi^+ : ( \alpha , \xi_i ) < 0} \tau_\alpha.$$ This is the same construction as the Jucys-Murphy elements for $S_n$. We have just replaced transpositions with pseudo-transpositions.
nodes.statement_short: $M_i$ is the sum of the pseudo-transpositions $\tau_\alpha$ over positive roots with $(\alpha,\xi_i)<0$.
differentia: the same construction as the Jucys-Murphy elements for $S_n$ with transpositions replaced by pseudo-transpositions

nodes.name: the module $V_\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let $V_\lambda$ denote any genuine projective $\tilde{S}_n$-module which has character corresponding to $\lambda \in \mathcal{SP}(n)$.

nodes.name: the function $q(m) = m(m+1)$
nodes.statement: It will be useful, for notation, to introduce a function $q:\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ such that $q(m) = m(m+1)$.

nodes.name: the spectrum data $\Sspec(n)$ and $\Sspec(n,\lambda)$
nodes.statement: We say $\alpha = (\alpha_1,\ldots ,\alpha_n)$ is in $\Sspec(n)$ if there exists a vector $v$ in an irreducible genuine projective representation $V$ of $\tilde{S}_n$ such that: $$M_k^2 v = \frac{1}{2}q(a_k) v \text{ for all } k=1,\ldots ,n.$$ $\Sspec(n, \lambda)$ is the restriction of $\Sspec(n)$ by considering vectors in any $V_\lambda$, $\lambda \in \mathcal{SP}(n)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Sspec(n)$ collects the vectors of joint $M_k^2$-eigenvalues $\frac12 q(a_k)$ occurring on irreducible genuine projective representations.
differentia: there exists a vector $v$ in an irreducible genuine projective representation $V$ of $\tilde{S}_n$ such that $M_k^2 v = \frac{1}{2}q(a_k) v \text{ for all } k=1,\ldots ,n$

nodes.name: content of a box in a shifted Young diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda \in \mathcal{SP}(n)$ be a shifted partition.The content of a box $(i,j)$ contained in a shifted Young diagram $\lambda$ is its distance from the main diagonal. $$\cont(i,j) = j-i$$
nodes.genus: its distance from the main diagonal
differentia: $(i,j)$ contained in a shifted Young diagram $\lambda$

nodes.name: the set of shifted content vectors $\Scont(n)$
nodes.statement: We introduce the set of shifted content vectors $\Scont(n)$. A vector $\beta = (\beta_1,\ldots ,\beta_n)$ is associated to a standard shifted tableaux $[[\lambda]]$ if, for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$, $\beta_i$ is equal to the content of the box labelled i in $[[\lambda]]$. $\Scont(n)$ is the set of vectors which are associated to a standard shifted tableau of size n. Similarly $\Scont(n,\lambda)$, is the set of vectors associated to standard shifted tableaux of shape $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Scont(n)$ is the set of content vectors of standard shifted tableaux of size $n$ (and $\Scont(n,\lambda)$ those of shape $\lambda$).
nodes.genus: the set of shifted content vectors
differentia: the set of vectors which are associated to a standard shifted tableau of size n
$\beta_i$ is equal to the content of the box labelled i in $[[\lambda]]$

nodes.name: central character of $\mathbb{H}$ and the element $\nu$
nodes.statement: A central character is a map $Z(\mathbb{H}) = S(V)^W \to \mathbb{C}$. The standard representations $X_\lambda$ have central characters $\chi_\lambda$. The vector space $\Hom(S(V)^W, \mathbb{C})$ can be associated with $V^*/W$ via evaluating polynomials in $S(V)/W$ at an element in $V^*/W$. Hence a central character, $\chi$, corresponds to an element $\nu \in V^*/W$.
nodes.statement_short: A central character is a map $Z(\mathbb{H}) = S(V)^W\to\mathbb{C}$, equivalently a $W$-orbit $\nu \in V^*/W$.

nodes.name: the subalgebra $\langle M_1,\ldots ,M_n \rangle$
nodes.statement: Let $\langle M_1,\ldots ,M_n \rangle$ be the subalgebra of $\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]$ generated by the Jucys-Murphy elements $M_i$.

nodes.name: the intertwiner $P_{s_i}$
nodes.statement: If $\alpha$ and $s_i(\alpha)$ are in $\Sspec(n,\lambda)$ then define $P_{s_i}:V_\alpha \to V_{s_i(\alpha)}$ to be the vector space isomorphism such that $$M_{s_i(j)}^2 (P_{s_i} (v)) = P_{s_i} M_j v \text{ for all } v \in V_\alpha.$$
differentia: $M_{s_i(j)}^2 (P_{s_i} (v)) = P_{s_i} M_j v \text{ for all } v \in V_\alpha$

nodes.name: the action of $\tau_i$ on $V_\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let $V_\lambda = \sum_{\alpha \in \Sspec(n, \lambda)} V_\alpha$ as supermodules of $\langle M_1,\ldots ,M_n\rangle \subset \tilde{S}_n$. Let $\alpha = (\alpha_1,\ldots ,\alpha_n) \in \Sspec(n, \lambda)$. The action of $\tau_i$, on $V_\alpha$ is defined in the following way. If $s_i(\alpha) \in \Sspec(n)$ then, $$\tau_i = \frac{M_i - M_{i+1}}{q(a_i) -q(a_{i+1})}- \left(1 - \frac{q(a_i) +q(a_{i+1})}{(q(a_i) - q(a_{i+1}))^2}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} P_{s_i} .$$ If $s_i(\alpha ) \notin \Sspec(n, \lambda)$ then $(1 - \frac{q(a_i) +q(a_{i+1})}{(q(a_i) - q(a_{i+1})^2}))= 0$ and on $V_\alpha$, $$\tau_i = \frac{M_i - M_{i+1}}{q(a_i) -q(a_{i+1})}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Builds $V_\lambda$ from the spectrum data by declaring $\tau_i$ to act by a Jucys-Murphy rational expression plus a normalised intertwiner $P_{s_i}$ when $s_i(\alpha)$ is again spectral.

nodes.name: Vogan's morphism $\zeta$ for graded Hecke algebras
nodes.statement: Vogan's morphism for graded Hecke algebras is the algebra homomorphism $\zeta: Z(\mathbb{H}) \to Z(\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n])$ defined such that $\zeta(z)$ for $z \in Z(\mathbb{H})$ is the unique element in $Z(\tilde{S}_n)$ such that $$z\otimes 1 = \rho (\zeta(z)) + Da + aD$$ as elements of $\mathbb{H} \otimes C(V)$, for some $a \in \mathbb{H}\otimes C(V)$. This morphism was introduced in \cite{BCT12} and is inspired by Vogan's morphism for real reductive groups. It occurs naturally in Dirac theory for graded Hecke algebras but as far as the author is aware it has not been described unlike in Dirac theory for real reductive groups.
nodes.statement_short: $\zeta: Z(\mathbb{H}) \to Z(\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n])$ sends $z$ to the unique central element with $z\otimes 1 = \rho(\zeta(z)) + Da + aD$.
nodes.definiendum: Vogan's morphism for graded Hecke algebras
differentia: $\zeta(z)$ is the unique element in $Z(\tilde{S}_n)$ such that $z\otimes 1 = \rho (\zeta(z)) + Da + aD$ as elements of $\mathbb{H} \otimes C(V)$, for some $a \in \mathbb{H}\otimes C(V)$

nodes.name: the projected Vogan morphism $\underline{\zeta}$
nodes.statement: We will describe $$\underline{\zeta}: Z(\mathbb{H}) \to Z(\mathcal{T}_n).$$ This is $\zeta$ composed with the projection from $\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]$ to $\mathcal{T}_n$.
differentia: $\zeta$ composed with the projection from $\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]$ to $\mathcal{T}_n$

nodes.name: the dual map $\underline{\zeta}^*$
nodes.statement: The dual map $\underline{\zeta}^*$ takes the irreducible representations of $\mathcal{T}_n$ to central characters of $\mathbb{H}$. Let $\sigma \in \irr(\mathcal{T}_n)$ and let $p \in Z(\mathbb{H})$. The central character $\underline{\zeta}^* (\sigma): Z(\mathbb{H}) \to \mathbb{C}$ is $$ \underline{\zeta}^*(\sigma)(f) = \sigma(\underline{\zeta}(p)).$$
nodes.statement_short: $\underline{\zeta}^*$ pulls an irreducible $\mathcal{T}_n$-representation back to a central character of $\mathbb{H}$.
differentia: takes the irreducible representations of $\mathcal{T}_n$ to central characters of $\mathbb{H}$

nodes.name: the central power polynomials $P^{2m}_{\mathcal{T}_n}$ and $P^{2m}_{\mathbb{H}}$
nodes.statement: Let $M_i$ be the Jucys-Murphy elements for $\mathcal{T}_n$. We define, $$P_{\mathcal{T}_n}^{2m} = \sum_{i=1}^n (2M_i)^{2m} \in Z(\mathcal{T}_n)_{\even}.$$ The set $\{\xi_1,..,\xi_n\}$ is an orthogonal basis of $V$. Define $$P_{\mathbb{H}}^{2m} = \sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor \frac{m}{2} \rfloor} {{m}\choose{2j}} \sum_{i=1}^n (2x_i)^{2m-2j}\in Z(\mathbb{H})_{\even}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Matching central elements: an even power sum of the $2M_i$ in $Z(\mathcal{T}_n)$ and a binomially weighted even power sum of the $2x_i$ in $Z(\mathbb{H})$.

nodes.name: the sets $\mathcal{P}^1$ and $\mathcal{P}^1_n$
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{P}^1$ to be the set of partitions, of any number, of length 1. $\mathcal{P}^1_n$ is the singleton subset of $\mathcal{P}^1$, consisting of the partition $\lambda = (n).$
nodes.genus: the set of partitions, of any number
differentia: $\mathcal{P}^1_n$ is the singleton subset consisting of the partition $\lambda = (n)$

nodes.name: Theorem A (branching rules for genuine projective irreducible $\tilde{S}_n$-supermodules)
nodes.statement: The branching rules of the genuine projective irreducible $\tilde{S}_n$-supermodules are: $$Res^{n}_{n-1} \tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \begin{cases} 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is odd and } \lambda_r = 1, \\ 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is odd and } \lambda_r > 1, \\ \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is even.}\end{cases}$$ Here $\lambda$ is always a strict partition.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction of $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ to $\tilde{S}_{n-1}$ is the sum of the $\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(i)}}$, with multiplicity $2$ exactly when $n-r$ is odd (the last summand being simple iff $\lambda_r=1$).
assumptions: Here $\lambda$ is always a strict partition.

nodes.name: Theorem B ($\Sspec(n) = \Scont(n)$)
nodes.statement: The set $\Sspec(n) \subset \mathbb{N}^n$, descending from eigenvalues of Jucys-Murphy elements, is equal to the set $\Scont(n)$, a combinatorial construction from contents of shifted Young tableaux. Further, $$\Sspec(n,\lambda) \cong \Scont(n,\lambda).$$
nodes.statement_short: Jucys-Murphy spectrum data for $\tilde{S}_n$ coincides with content data of standard shifted Young tableaux, shape by shape.
assumptions: The set $\Sspec(n) \subset \mathbb{N}^n$, descending from eigenvalues of Jucys-Murphy elements
conclusions: is equal to the set $\Scont(n)$, a combinatorial construction from contents of shifted Young tableaux

nodes.name: Theorem C (surjectivity of Vogan's map onto the even centre)
nodes.statement: Vogan's map projected onto the group algebra $\mathcal{T}_n \cong \tilde{S}_n/ \langle z +1 \rangle$, $\underline{\zeta}: Z(\mathbb{H}) \to Z[\mathcal{T}_n]$, is surjective onto the even part of the centre. Also $\underline{\zeta}$ kills all odd polynomials in $Z(\mathbb{H})$.
nodes.statement_short: $\underline{\zeta}$ surjects onto $Z(\mathcal{T}_n)_{\even}$ and annihilates the odd polynomials.
assumptions: Vogan's map projected onto the group algebra $\mathcal{T}_n \cong \tilde{S}_n/ \langle z +1 \rangle$, $\underline{\zeta}: Z(\mathbb{H}) \to Z[\mathcal{T}_n]$
conclusions: is surjective onto the even part of the centre

nodes.name: Morris' presentation of the double cover $\tilde{W}$
nodes.statement: The double cover $\tilde{W}$ of $W$ admits a presentation akin to Coxeter presentations for a Weyl group, $$\tilde{W} = \langle z , \tilde{s}_\alpha \text{ for all } \alpha \in \Pi : z^2 = 1, (\tilde{s}_\alpha \tilde{s}_\beta) ^{m(\alpha,\beta)} = z^{m(\alpha,\beta)-1}, z \text{ is central } \rangle$$ where $m(\alpha, \alpha) =1$ and $m(\alpha,\beta) = \langle \alpha , \beta \rangle \langle \beta , \alpha \rangle+ 2$.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde{W}$ has a Coxeter-like presentation on $z$ and lifts $\tilde{s}_\alpha$ of the simple reflections, with braid relations twisted by powers of the central $z$.
assumptions: The double cover $\tilde{W}$ of $W$
$m(\alpha, \alpha) =1$ and $m(\alpha,\beta) = \langle \alpha , \beta \rangle \langle \beta , \alpha \rangle+ 2$
conclusions: $\tilde{W} = \langle z , \tilde{s}_\alpha \text{ for all } \alpha \in \Pi : z^2 = 1, (\tilde{s}_\alpha \tilde{s}_\beta) ^{m(\alpha,\beta)} = z^{m(\alpha,\beta)-1}, z \text{ is central } \rangle$

nodes.name: Parthasarathy-type formula $\mathcal{D}^2 = \Omega_\mathbb{H}\otimes 1- \rho(\Omega_{\tilde{S_n}})$
nodes.statement: As elements of $\mathbb{H}\otimes C(V)$, $$\mathcal{D}^2 = \Omega_\mathbb{H}\otimes 1- \rho(\Omega_{\tilde{S_n}}),$$
nodes.statement_short: The square of the Dirac element is the difference of the two Casimirs.
assumptions: As elements of $\mathbb{H}\otimes C(V)$

nodes.name: Garcia-Procesi branching for the graded character $p^\lambda(\textbf{q})$
nodes.statement: The restriction of the $S_n$ $\textbf{q}$-graded character $p^\lambda(\textbf{q})$ to $S_{n-1}$ is a sum of $\textbf{q}^{i-1}p^{\lambda^{(i)}}(\textbf{q})$; $$\Res^n_{n-1}p^\lambda(\textbf{q}) = \sum_{i=1}^{l(\lambda)} \textbf{q}^{i-1} p^{\lambda^{(i)}}(\textbf{q}).$$
assumptions: The restriction of the $S_n$ $\textbf{q}$-graded character $p^\lambda(\textbf{q})$ to $S_{n-1}$

nodes.name: branching rules for the genuine projective irreducible $\tilde{S}_n$-supermodules
nodes.statement: The branching rules of the genuine projective irreducible $\tilde{S}_n$-supermodules are $$Res^{n}_{n-1} \tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \begin{cases} 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is odd and } \lambda_r = 1, \\ 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus 2\tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is odd and } \lambda_r > 1, \\ \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(2)}}\oplus \ldots \oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r-1)}}\oplus \tilde{\tau}_{\lambda^{(r)}} & \text{ if } n-r \text{ is even.}\end{cases}$$ Here $\lambda$ is always a strict partition.
nodes.statement_short: The full branching graph of $\mathcal{T}_n$: multiplicities are $2$ when $n-r$ is odd, $1$ when $n-r$ is even, with the $\lambda_r=1$ exception in the last summand.
assumptions: Here $\lambda$ is always a strict partition.

nodes.name: spectrum data equals content data
nodes.statement: The set $\Sspec(n) \subset \mathbb{N}^n$ is equal to the set $\Scont(n)$. Further, $$\Sspec(n,\lambda) = \Scont(n,\lambda).$$
nodes.statement_short: $\Sspec(n)=\Scont(n)$, and shape-by-shape $\Sspec(n,\lambda)=\Scont(n,\lambda)$.
assumptions: The set $\Sspec(n) \subset \mathbb{N}^n$

nodes.name: $\{V_\lambda\}$ is a full set of representatives of the irreducible genuine projective supermodules
nodes.statement: For the set of shifted tableaux $\mathcal{SP}(n)$, $\{V_\lambda: \lambda \in \mathcal{SP}(n)\}$ is a full set of representatives of the irreducible genuine projective supermodules of $\tilde{S}_n$.
assumptions: For the set of shifted tableaux $\mathcal{SP}(n)$
conclusions: $\{V_\lambda: \lambda \in \mathcal{SP}(n)\}$ is a full set of representatives of the irreducible genuine projective supermodules of $\tilde{S}_n$

nodes.statement: For $m, n\in \mathbb{N}$ and for all shifted $\lambda$, $$\sigma_\lambda(P_{\mathcal{T}_n}^{2m}) = \chi_\lambda(P_{\mathbb{H}}^{2m}).$$
nodes.statement_short: The two families of central power polynomials act identically on every $V_\lambda$.
assumptions: For $m, n\in \mathbb{N}$ and for all shifted $\lambda$

nodes.name: matching actions for partitions of length one
nodes.statement: Let $\mu \in \mathcal{P}^1$ be a partition of length one then, for all $m \in \mathbb{N}$, $$\sigma_\mu(P_{\mathcal{T}_n}^{2m}) = \chi_\mu (P_{\mathbb{H}}^{2m}).$$
assumptions: Let $\mu \in \mathcal{P}^1$ be a partition of length one
for all $m \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Dirac index as a tensor product (exactness)
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module. The Dirac index can be expressed as a tensor, $I_\#(X) = X \otimes (\mathcal{S}^+ - \mathcal{S}^-).$ Hence it is exact. Furthermore for $w \in \tilde{W}'$, $$ tr(w, I_\#(X)) = tr(p(w),X)tr(w,S^+ - S^-).$$
nodes.statement_short: $I_\#(X) = X\otimes(\mathcal{S}^+-\mathcal{S}^-)$, so the index functor is exact and its character factors as a product of traces.
assumptions: Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module
for $w \in \tilde{W}'$

nodes.name: construction of $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ and the constant $a_\lambda$
nodes.statement: For every strict partition $\lambda$ of $n$, let $\mathcal{S}$ be an ungraded spinor module and $X_{-1}(\lambda)$ be the graded module of $S_n$ corresponding to $\lambda$. Define the $\tilde{S}_n$-module, $$\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \frac{1}{a_\lambda} X_{-1}(\lambda) \otimes S,$$ where $$a_\lambda = \begin{cases} 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)}{2}} & n \text{ even and } l(\lambda) \text{ even}, \\ 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-1}{2}} & l(\lambda) \text{ odd}, \\ 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-2}{2}} & n \text{ odd and } l(\lambda) \text{ even}. \end{cases}$$ If $n-l(\lambda)$ is even then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is an irreducible $\sgn$ self-dual $\tilde{S}_n$-module. If $n-l(\lambda)$ is odd then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \tilde{\tau}^+_\lambda + \tilde{\tau}^-_\lambda$, with $\tilde{\tau}^\pm_\lambda$ irreducible modules which are $\sgn$ dual to each other.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda := a_\lambda^{-1} X_{-1}(\lambda)\otimes S$ is irreducible and $\sgn$ self-dual when $n-l(\lambda)$ is even, and splits into a $\sgn$-dual pair when odd.
assumptions: For every strict partition $\lambda$ of $n$, let $\mathcal{S}$ be an ungraded spinor module and $X_{-1}(\lambda)$ be the graded module of $S_n$ corresponding to $\lambda$
$a_\lambda = 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)}{2}}$ if $n$ even and $l(\lambda)$ even, $2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-1}{2}}$ if $l(\lambda)$ odd, $2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-2}{2}}$ if $n$ odd and $l(\lambda)$ even
conclusions: If $n-l(\lambda)$ is even then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is an irreducible $\sgn$ self-dual $\tilde{S}_n$-module

nodes.name: isomorphism classes of $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ are labelled by nilpotent orbits
nodes.statement: Two $\textbf{q}$-graded $S_n$-modules $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ and $X_{\textbf{q}}(e')$ are isomorphic if and only if $e$ is in the same conjugacy class as $e'$. Hence the isomorphism classes of $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ can labelled by nilpotent orbits, these are equivalent to partitions of $n$. We write the isomorphism class of $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ as $X_{\textbf{q}}(\lambda)$ where $e$ has Jordan form corresponding to a partition $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)\cong X_{\textbf{q}}(e')$ iff $e,e'$ are conjugate, so the classes are indexed by partitions and written $X_{\textbf{q}}(\lambda)$.
assumptions: Two $\textbf{q}$-graded $S_n$-modules $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ and $X_{\textbf{q}}(e')$
conclusions: are isomorphic if and only if $e$ is in the same conjugacy class as $e'$

nodes.name: reduction rule on strict partitions removes a box from row $i$
nodes.statement: For a strict partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r) \vdash n$ we have $$\lambda^{(i)} = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_{i-1},\lambda_{i} -1 , \lambda_{i+1},\ldots ,\lambda_r).$$ Hence $\{\lambda^{(i)} : i =1,\ldots ,l(\lambda) \}$ is equal to the set $\Theta^n_{n-1}(\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_short: For strict $\lambda$ the Garcia-Procesi rule just subtracts one from the $i$th part, so it produces exactly all single-box removals.
assumptions: For a strict partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r) \vdash n$
conclusions: $\{\lambda^{(i)} : i =1,\ldots ,l(\lambda) \}$ is equal to the set $\Theta^n_{n-1}(\lambda)$

nodes.name: restriction of $X_{\textbf{q}}(\lambda)$

assumptions: Let $\lambda$ be a strict partition

nodes.name: action of $\Omega_\mathbb{H}$ on $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ via contents
nodes.statement: On the representation $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ corresponding to $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r)$, $$\Omega_\mathbb{H} = \sum_{i=1}^{l(\lambda)} \sum_{j=1}^{\lambda_i} (\frac{2j - \lambda_i}{2})^2.$$ Furthermore, this can be reformulated in terms of the content of $\lambda$, $$ \Omega_\mathbb{H} =\frac{1}{4} \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} q(\cont(i,j)).$$

Then the the representation $U$ of $\langle M_1,\ldots ,M_n \rangle$ factors through the Clifford algebra of rank $r$, where $r = |\{M_i^2 \text{ with non zero eigenvalue}\}| = n - l(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: hook length formula for shifted tableaux
nodes.statement: The hook length formula for shifted tableaux gives an explicit description for the number of standard shifted tableaux for a shifted partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r\} \vDash n$, $$\# \{\text{ standard shifted tableaux of shape }\lambda\} = \frac{n!}{\lambda_1!\ldots \lambda_r!} \prod_{i=1}^{r} \frac{\lambda_i - \lambda_j}{\lambda_i +\lambda_j}.$$
